meta.name: Ontology Drift Guardrails
meta.authority: Owner-directed 2026-11-17; codified permanent rules; no drift permitted
meta.enforcement_summary: Rule 11 weekly pg_cron invalid-index sweep (SHMT migration 20261117204505); Rule 12 weekly GitHub Actions ontology tracker + receipt-silence alarm (ontology-control.yml)

rules.title: No out-of-band schema applies
rules.text: All SQL that changes schema ships through the slot system: `reserve → write file → bind (sha256 + commit) → PR → merge → apply`. Break-glass (`ops.allow_unbound_ledger_apply`) is for incidents only, is logged as `break_glass_unbound_apply`, and **requires a retroactive archive stub PR within 24 hours**. *Mechanism: RS003 ledger trigger + RS-1 monotonicity guard + drift check. Verified: four out-of-band fleet applies in Nov 2026 each blocked all PRs until stubbed (#3817, #3836, and the two carried on #3820).*

rules.title: Reissues must be additive
rules.text: Never delete or rename an already-applied migration's file when reissuing. The ledger records history; the repo must mirror it exactly. *Mechanism: the version-uniqueness check ("already-applied history was deleted/renamed; restore its exact path"). Learned: PR #3937 repaired exactly this.*

rules.title: Merge and apply in the same session
rules.text: A bound slot's version goes backdated the moment the ledger high-water mark moves past it. The gap between merge and apply is the risk window — hours, not days. *Mechanism: RS-1 refuses backdated versions. Learned: three D6 reissues (20261110164033, 20261111093802, 20261111114323) went stale in the window; the fourth was applied minutes after merge.*

rules.title: Archive before drop; verify before delete
rules.text: Every purge candidate gets a full compressed pg_dump archived to private release assets with a manifest (exact row counts + sha256), and the manifest is verified against the live database and the asset checksum byte-for-byte BEFORE anything is dropped. The archive is the permanent restore path. *Mechanism: the d6-archive workflow pattern (d6-archive + d6-phase3-rent-observations releases). Verified: phase-0 archive verified before the phase-1 drops; the phase-3 archive verified byte-for-byte (39,912,418 rows).*

rules.title: Verify with live counts, never catalog stats
rules.text: `pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup` is unreliable on never-analyzed tables. Purge decisions require real `COUNT(*)` on the candidate table. *Learned: "1.3 GB of empty-table bloat" was actually 5.3M live rows across three tables; the truncate was aborted at the verification step.*

rules.title: "Unused" requires proof of no active reads AND duplication
rules.text: A table is purgeable only if ALL hold: (a) zero meaningful scans, (b) no view/function/cron/workflow references (including dynamic SQL in view definitions — pg_depend misses those), (c) its content is duplicated in actively-read tables, (d) a fleet reference check of repo code. Otherwise it is pipeline data. *Learned: pdi.\*_parcels_stage looked cold but is the live national-parcel ingest path (promotion ran the same morning).*

rules.title: Protected data classes (never purge candidates)
rules.text: Historical wayback captures (archived rent evidence for Comptrove) and all parcel product data (pdi/spine parcel tables) are protected. Old observations leave the hot DB only via the partition-and-archive path (Rule 4 discipline), never via purge.

rules.title: Fleet out-of-band applies file their own stubs same-day
rules.text: The drift check blocks every PR in the repo until each unarchived applied version has its exact file on main (verbatim from the authoring repo, digest-matched to the slot). The retroactive archive pattern is the sanctioned repair; the quality session may perform it when the fleet is slow, always with the fleet's original bytes. *Mechanism: check_migration_drift.py + DEPLOY-HARDEN-1 (checkout-lag re-check against latest main).*

rules.title: Stale-slot hygiene
rules.text: Bound-but-never-applied slots (superseded reissues) are flagged for the fleet's stale-slot cleanup pattern and must not accumulate. Current known: 20261110164033, 20261117055340.

rules.title: One-time jobs clean up after themselves
rules.text: Any one-time catch-up/fix job (e.g., the photo-sync catch-up, job 3186) must be unscheduled immediately after its success is verified. No orphaned one-time schedules. *Verified: the catch-up ran 19:47–19:50 UTC 2026-11-17 and was removed within minutes.*

rules.title: Invalid-index hygiene
rules.text: Interrupted concurrent index builds leave `indisvalid=FALSE` corpses. A weekly sweep drops or rebuilds them. Current known set: the `spine.parcel_upi_phcand_idx_ccnew*` series and `public.idx_tax_delinq_property_year` (38 total). *Mechanism: a simple pg_index query; candidate for a fleet cron.*

rules.title: Ontology receipt cadence is a monitored SLA
rules.text: The `shmt_ontology_control` tracker receipt (ops.ontology_tracker_receipt) must land on its schedule. **Currently breached: last receipt 2026-10-25 (23 days)** while the dataset registry itself updates daily — the report layer, not the data, went quiet. This is the one open ontology-universe gap: the fleet must restore the ontology_control run cadence or the owner is notified.
